extracted.intended_audience: architects, art historians, students of architecture, and educated readers interested in Venetian/Byzantine architecture
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines and principles for judging and composing incrusted (brick-faced-with-precious-stone) Byzantine/Venetian architecture, illustrated through St. Mark's; includes formal architectural criteria and assessment of fitness for worship/expression.

rubrics_metrics.name: Incrustation as the building's root characteristic
rubrics_metrics.description: The first broad characteristic of the building, and the root nearly of every other important peculiarity in it, is its confessed 'incrustation'. It is the purest example in Italy of the school in which the ruling principle is the incrustation of brick with more precious materials.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognize that in incrusted buildings the structural body is brick and the external surface is a distinct 'armor' of marble/colored stones; judge arrangements with that duplicity in mind rather than against expectations from massive stone construction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinction between incrusted and massive styles
rubrics_metrics.description: There are two generally distinct families of buildings: one in which the substance is alike throughout (massive), and the other in which the substance is of two kinds, internal and external (incrusted).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Form decisively distinct ideas of legitimate characteristics of each style; intermediate examples exist but should not confuse the evaluation of a building belonging primarily to one school or the other.

rubrics_metrics.name: Legitimacy / honesty of incrusted construction (not insincerity)
rubrics_metrics.description: The incrusted school appears insincere to a Northern builder but is not intended to deceive; every slab of facial marble is fastened by a confessed 'rivet', and the joints are visibly accommodated to the contours within.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess honesty by looking for visible means of attachment (rivets, binding courses) and clear separation of armor from structure; do not criticize as deceptive where constructional methods and customs explain the appearance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Natural/material circumstances should justify style
rubrics_metrics.description: The adoption of the incrusted method is naturally influenced by absence of local quarries, precarious access to mainland stone, and the economics/limits of sea transport.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate stylistic choices in light of practical constraints (availability, shipping, sizes of marble), and consider these circumstances legitimate reasons for using incrustation rather than as faults.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preservation and respectful reuse of ancient fragments
rubrics_metrics.description: Given scarcity and the availability of sculptured fragments from ruins, the architect may either mutilate old marbles to fit new designs or preserve and insert them; the Venetian choice was to save every relic.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Value saving and displaying noble existing works within new construction as an ethical and aesthetic principle; prefer incorporation of intact fragments over invasive alteration for mere display of skill.

rubrics_metrics.name: Importance of color-perception in judging incrusted architecture
rubrics_metrics.description: The very first requisite for true judgment of St. Mark's is the perfection of that color-faculty; the school of incrusted architecture is the only one in which perfect and permanent chromatic decoration is possible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a critic lacks perception or delight in color, they cannot fairly judge the merits of such a building; assess the building's chromatic composition as a primary criterion, not secondary ornament.

rubrics_metrics.name: Twofold inquiry: judge formally then expressively
rubrics_metrics.description: First judge a building merely as a work of art (construction and decorative merit), and secondly estimate its fitness for its special duty as a place of worship (expressional purposes).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Separate formal/technical evaluation from the question of how well the building fulfills its intended religious or social functions; both inquiries are necessary for a full judgment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assessment of ornament as 'cakes of very hard color' applied to a brick body
rubrics_metrics.description: Every piece of jasper and alabaster should be looked upon as a 'cake of very hard color' to paint walls with; accept that the body/strength of the edifice is in brick, clothed with marble armor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Read ornament primarily as chromatic surface treatment bonded to a brick structure; judge proportions, patterning, and the fitting of colored stones as one would judge a color composition, with attention to how surface pieces relate to the substratum.

rubrics_metrics.name: LAW I — Plinths and cornices for binding the armor must be light and delicate
rubrics_metrics.description: "That the plinths and cornices used for binding the armor are to be light and delicate." Covering pieces require a thickness (at least two or three inches) to prevent fracture; they must be connected with the mass by binding cornices and string courses and not relied upon solely on cement or rivets.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure binding plinths/string courses visibly perform binding/support functions but are proportioned so as not to be mistaken for primary structural elements; they should be too slight to take important structural work and must secure mutual support of facing pieces rather than act as main load-bearers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recognition of decorative accumulation from spoil vs coherent architectural order
rubrics_metrics.description: The front of St. Mark's became 'rather a shrine at which to dedicate the splendor of miscellaneous spoil, than the organized expression of any fixed architectural law or religious emotion.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When evaluating, distinguish between splendor born of accumulated trophies/fragments and splendor arising from organized architectural conception; judge whether assemblage of materials serves coherent design or merely displays wealth/trophies.
